old_caption: The video captures a close-up view of a wet pavement, likely after rainfall or a spill. The surface is dark gray, speckled with small debris such as leaves and seeds. A significant amount of water has pooled, reflecting light and creating a glossy sheen. In the center of the frame, a white object, possibly a piece of paper or a small plastic item, lies partially submerged in the water. The water level remains static throughout the sequence, with the white object staying in the same position. The background features a textured wall with a dark, rectangular vent or grate, adding depth to the scene. The overall atmosphere suggests a quiet, possibly urban setting, with the focus on the interplay between the water and the surrounding environment.

caption: The video captures a low-angle, shallow-focus view of a wet asphalt surface. In the foreground-left lies a dark, irregular puddle whose center-right carries a bright silvery-white reflection of the sky. Solid debris sits at the puddle's edge, a small brown nut at left-center and a tiny fragment right of the highlight, while a curved orange-brown husk rests on the dry mid-right ground. The background is a blurred wooden wall with a dark square panel left and a small green sprout near center. Throughout the excerpt the bright reflection slowly deforms, reading as a taller rounded highlight early on and becoming flatter and more horizontally spread. The dark wet contour shifts slightly with it, appearing to extend a touch toward the right. The foreground asphalt and puddle edges vary a little in apparent sharpness across the frames. All solid objects—the husk, the fragments, the sprout, and the panel—stay in essentially fixed positions relative to the frame.

Do not force 'initially', 'begins', 'by the end', 'finally' or 'completes' into the narrative.
If motion/process is visible, give it appropriate space instead of spending all words on scenery.
Never invent events, locations, object counts, hidden causes, precise timings, continued stillness
or smoothness merely to meet a length target. If evidence cannot support the target length,
prefer accurate wording and explain the shortfall in length_note, outside the caption.
Finish every sentence. Avoid redundant atmospheric padding and unsupported 'likely' guesses.
